I was a firefighter / E.M.T. for a subcontracting crew. I worked wild land forest fires such as the Big Bar complex. It was in the job description when I applied.

Though a WLFF is a far cry from traditional firefighters.

I'm a FF on A-shift and an EMT on B-shift. I love both jobs, but they are two different jobs. I feel like fire and EMS should be separate, but EMS (at least in my area) needs significant improvement before that can happen. We have 14 engines and 5 ambulances. It makes no sense.

In departments where fire and EMS are the same department, your best, most motivated, ambitious FF can get his paramedic numbers and because of the rarity of medics, never fight fire again. He gets stuck on an ambulance as a "FF/medic" and works the rest of his career as a medic with a hemlet. It's wasteful, and breeds resentment. The most dangerous thing in this line of work is complacency, and that's a path straight to it.

I think the best way to deal with this is to have EMS if the department wants it, but everyone should be informed when they apply that they are taking a position as an EMT or medic; NOT a FF. if a FF has his medic numbers he can sub in when need be, but you have to let a certified FF be a FF when he works for the fire department.

That's my take, at least. It's an ongoing debate throughout the fire service as a whole, and I'm sure it will be for a long time.
